text:
Maria (Support): @jon Eng-SRE — urgent escal from AcmeMaps. Their production traffic (region=eu-west) started seeing >2min p50 and lots of 502/401s. Customer says requests are being routed to us-west intermittently. Suspect multi-region heartbeat flip triggered fallback. Samples + repro below, billing impact possible (they showed token usage spike).

Maria (Support): repro steps from customer:
1) Send steady traffic to eu-west endpoint with client header X-Region: eu-west
2) Observe 502/401 bursts ~12:34-12:38 UTC and increased RTTs

Logs (scrubbed):
```
[2026-03-16T12:33:58Z] route_decision tenant=acme-maps request_id=tr-9a8b kernel=us-west chosen=true reason=fallback_healthy_check_down
[2026-03-16T12:34:05Z] auth error tenant=acme-maps request_id=tr-9a8b status=401 token_expired=false msg="upstream returned 502"
[2026-03-16T12:34:30Z] heartbeat probe eu-west state=DOWN count=3 last=2026-03-16T12:34:29Z
[2026-03-16T12:35:12Z] route_decision tenant=acme-maps request_id=tr-9a8c kernel=eu-west chosen=true reason=healthy
```

Jon (Eng-SRE): thanks — can you paste a request trace id (full) and the routing metadata from the proxy for one of the failing requests? Also capture the healthcheck time series (last 30m) for eu-west.

Maria (Support): trace_id=tr-9a8b-0001 (attached APM link: https://apm.redwood.example/trace/tr-9a8b-0001)
Routing metadata snippet: tenant=acme-maps prefer_region=eu-west fallback_regions=[us-west,us-east] routing_policy=client-affinity ttl=300

deploy-bot: :warning: Healthcheck flip detected for cluster eu-west at 2026-03-16T12:34:29Z — status changed DOWN -> UP -> DOWN within 90s. Probe failure rate 0.42

Kevin (Platform): FYI I rolled out a probe sensitivity tweak to the probe scaler ~12:00 UTC (reduced success threshold from 4 -> 3 consecutive successes) to speed up failback. That can make transient noise appear as flaps. Reverting now. For immediate mitigation: we should pin acme-maps to eu-west and disable cross-region fallback for their tenant until we stabilize.

Jon (Eng-SRE): agree. Action plan: 1) revert probe sensitivity change (Kevin) 2) apply tenant override prefer_region=eu-west + disable_fallback=true (Platform) 3) widen healthcheck window to 2m for eu-west (Eng-SRE) 4) monitor and roll back if errors persist.

Kevin (Platform): running commands now:
```
# revert sensitivity
infractl probes update eu-west --min-success 4 --apply
# tenant override
infractl tenants set acme-maps --prefer-region eu-west --disable-fallback true
```
Outputs: apply ok, tenant override ok.

Olivia (CSM): Heads up — AcmeMaps is on a paid SL/commit. They already saw a surge in token usage while traffic bounced. Recommend we offer a billing credit for the impacted window and send a PPT with RCA once fixed. I'll draft customer comms. :+1:

Maria (Support): added a repro curl (customer):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Region: eu-west" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
When the routing bounce happened that same call showed 401 with body: {"error":"upstream_auth_failure"}.

Jon (Eng-SRE): confirmed in the routing logs that requests with the tenant header were still being evaluated for fallback when the probe briefly reported DOWN. Looks like the decision path treats probe DOWN as higher priority than tenant hint in current policy — that's the bug. I'll open an internal ticket to change policy ordering so tenant pinning + client affinity beats transient probe failures.

Maria (Support): ticket created ENG-8242 (priority P1). Temporary mitigation applied, customer pinned. Monitoring now.

Kevin (Platform): also bumping healthcheck window for eu-west:
```
infractl probes update eu-west --window 120s --apply
```

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: infra change applied: revert probe sensitivity + tenant override + window change at 2026-03-16T12:47Z

Maria (Support): will monitor with customer; asking for 2h watch and then we'll start RCA writeup. Olivia will handle billing note. Jon please add the routing policy change to ENG-8242.

Jon (Eng-SRE): adding notes to ENG-8242: reproduce steps, logs, decision-tree patch, unit tests, and a canary plan.

Olivia (CSM): I'll send a short note to the customer now: apologizing, explaining temporary mitigation, offering credit, and ETA for RCA.

Maria (Support): thanks all. Current status: mitigated (tenant pinned), monitoring. Will update thread if we see further flaps. :thumbsup:
